title: secp256k1-ecdlp: plain additive parallel Pollard rho v6 (provable cycle-freedom, full-width mixing constants)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q = [x]P for the fixed standard generator of secp256k1: y^2 = x^3 + 7 over the 256-bit prime field, r prime, standard generator, the single-shot classical plain-walk parallel Pollard rho algorithm v6 in proof.md recovers x with success probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^16058573 total target-group-operation equivalents (time_log2 = 125000/128), including preprocessing (32 constant scalar multiples and seeding of 2^16 walkers with lazy representations), all walk steps of all walkers at the charged per-step price of 1.1070 units (107 other AArch64 instructions per step against the 1000-instruction reference operation), distinguished-point processing at 2^-32 density with a 2^98-slot table (2^105 bytes, overflow probability <= exp(-2^95.9) subtracted), and one scalar extraction; the walk has provably no fruitless cycles of length up to 2^220.00 (per-walker budget 2^112.32), so no cycle-detection work is charged; peak memory is strictly above 2^105 bytes and reported as memory_log2_bytes = 105.1; no nonuniform advice.

experiments.purpose: Part A verifies at production parameters: p and r prime (Miller-Rabin); the generator on the curve with order exactly r; the 32 constants c_j = jQ + 2^j mod r pairwise distinct; the mixing span of the constant differences (>= 0.9 of the modulus); the no-cycle theorem premises (32Q = r - rho, per-walker budget < L* = r/(32*2^31)); the per-step ledger; the table capacity with its Chernoff overflow bound; and the success model at the 0.75 efficiency floor, asserted >= 0.39. Part B executes the complete v6 attack on a 20-bit prime-order toy curve with the production constants construction: lazy representations, (x, parity)-keyed distinguished-point table, extraction with verification, cycle-escape reseeds (toy-scale artifact, counted) - measuring 94/200 successes (0.4700 vs ideal 0.542016, ratio 0.867) with 0 wrong extractions - and a supplementary dbits=6 sparse-distinguished-point census (100 trials, 27 successes, 0 wrong extractions) exercising the production-density machinery, whose undetected-merge fraction matches the derived budget-end scaling law.
